## Rebuild the page, reuse the calculation

Quarto generates the site's HTML on every deployment. With the site-wide `execute: freeze: auto` setting, unchanged executable posts can reuse their committed `_freeze` results rather than repeating R or Python computations.

This repository also keeps `scripts/freeze-manifest.json`. **The manifest controls which extra packages need to be installed; Quarto controls whether frozen execution is reused.** These are related, but separate, decisions.

## The two decisions

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-cap: "Package-selection logic in the custom renderer; Quarto makes its own freeze decision later."
flowchart TD
    A["Inspect each .qmd"] --> B{"Explicit<br/>freeze: true?"}
    B -->|Yes| C{"Saved HTML<br/>execution result?"}
    C -->|No| X["Stop: required<br/>cluster output missing"]
    C -->|Yes| D["Skip this post's<br/>extra ci-packages"]
    B -->|No| E{"Saved result exists<br/>and source hash matches?"}
    E -->|Yes| D
    E -->|No| F["Include this post's<br/>extra ci-packages"]
    D --> G["Launch shared Pixi runtime"]
    F --> G
    G --> H["One Quarto render<br/>uses its own freeze rules"]
```

## Interactive: choose a document state

Try the cases below. This is a **client-side explanatory model** of the repository logic; it does not run a GitHub Actions job or modify any files.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof freezeCase = Inputs.select(
  [
    "Auto: unchanged document + matching cache",
    "Auto: document source changed",
    "Auto: saved freeze result missing",
    "Auto: manifest missing, freeze still exists",
    "Manual: freeze true + saved result",
    "Manual: freeze true + missing result"
  ],
  {label: "Choose the QMD and cache state:", value: "Auto: unchanged document + matching cache"}
)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
freezeOutcomes = ({
  "Auto: unchanged document + matching cache": {
    "Extra ci-packages": "Skip",
    "Quarto execution": "Reuse unchanged frozen computation",
    "Outcome": "Rebuild HTML; keep saved scientific results"
  },
  "Auto: document source changed": {
    "Extra ci-packages": "Include",
    "Quarto execution": "Reexecute changed document",
    "Outcome": "Generate updated freeze artifacts on success"
  },
  "Auto: saved freeze result missing": {
    "Extra ci-packages": "Include",
    "Quarto execution": "Execute without prior freeze",
    "Outcome": "Create fresh execution results"
  },
  "Auto: manifest missing, freeze still exists": {
    "Extra ci-packages": "Include",
    "Quarto execution": "May reuse unchanged freeze",
    "Outcome": "Manifest removal alone does not force execution"
  },
  "Manual: freeze true + saved result": {
    "Extra ci-packages": "Skip",
    "Quarto execution": "Reuse precomputed cluster results",
    "Outcome": "Site can publish without heavy runtime"
  },
  "Manual: freeze true + missing result": {
    "Extra ci-packages": "Not reached",
    "Quarto execution": "Not started",
    "Outcome": "Custom renderer stops with an error"
  }
})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
Inputs.table([freezeOutcomes[freezeCase]], {
  columns: ["Extra ci-packages", "Quarto execution", "Outcome"],
  rows: 1
})
```

## Automatic and manually frozen results

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Normal articles: `freeze: auto`

The project default is set in [`_quarto.yml`](https://github.com/YONGHUNI/blog/blob/main/_quarto.yml).

```yaml
execute:
  freeze: auto
```

If only an About page changes, Quarto still regenerates the website HTML, but unaffected cached scientific results can be reused.

### Cluster articles: `freeze: true`

For future CPU/GPU-intensive documents, an individual QMD can opt in:

```yaml
execute:
  freeze: true
```

The required `_freeze` output must first be computed and committed from the appropriate research environment. Whole-site CI refuses to continue if the expected saved HTML execution result is absent. Updating the data or code requires manually refreshing these frozen results.

### What gets committed?

After successful publishing, the workflow stages the manifest and generated auto-freeze files and commits them **only if the staged content changed**. Files under a manually frozen post's subtree are excluded from automatic staging.

The bot commit uses `[skip ci]` to avoid an unnecessary new publication run.

:::

## Cache maintenance

| Goal | Recommended action |
|---|---|
| Rebuild HTML only | Push the page change; keep `_freeze` |
| Recompute one ordinary post | Invalidate that post's saved execution result, then build |
| Recompute all ordinary posts | Remove their saved `_freeze` results, commit deletions, then build |
| Reset dependency fingerprinting | Reset `scripts/freeze-manifest.json`; this does **not** force Quarto execution |
| Update a manually frozen HPC post | Recompute the single document on the cluster and commit new frozen outputs |

::: {.callout-warning}
Do not wipe `_freeze` indiscriminately if you have posts using `freeze: true`. The renderer requires those externally produced results. Quarto's source-based freeze invalidation also does not detect every change to an external dataset or environment.
:::

**Relevant source:** [`scripts/render-site.py`](https://github.com/YONGHUNI/blog/blob/main/scripts/render-site.py) · [`scripts/freeze-manifest.json`](https://github.com/YONGHUNI/blog/blob/main/scripts/freeze-manifest.json)
